subject: A fictional coastal passage planner and on-water safety companion for small craft and the people waiting ashore
all_fictional: Brindlemouth harbour and all place names
the vessel Petrel and its crew
the weather models Nimbus-HR / Pelagic-9 / Coastal-Meso
every harbour notice, phone number and vessel on the noticeboard
computed_not_invented: tide curve and extremes (four-constituent harmonic sum)
stream speed and direction from the rate of rise
leg bearings and distances (great-circle on fictional coordinates)
fuel burn, reserve and margin arithmetic
drift datum, box radii, sweep times

steps.title: Dawn go/no-go card
steps.state_before: Evening before: a plan exists in the app but is not confirmed
steps.this_screen: GO with a 06:25 launch; float plan filed at 05:44
steps.what_it_hands_on: Confirms the plan and pushes it to the shore contact

steps.title: Tide and stream day chart
steps.state_before: The skipper trusts the app's verdict but wants the tide reasoning
steps.this_screen: Both bank windows and the required 2.50 m are on one screen
steps.what_it_hands_on: Sets the two crossing times in the plan

steps.title: Passage plan (A4, laminated)
steps.state_before: The plan exists digitally but the cockpit has no screen
steps.this_screen: A printed A4 plan with legs, ETAs, abort criteria and the escape route
steps.what_it_hands_on: Goes in the laminate pocket; becomes the document the crew actually flies

steps.title: Five-morning weather windows
steps.state_before: Four candidate mornings and no way to compare them
steps.this_screen: Saturday 06-09 is chosen; Sunday is cancelled; Monday is the fallback
steps.what_it_hands_on: Fixes the date that cases 01-03 are planned for

steps.title: Float plan and shore watch
steps.state_before: Someone ashore needs to know when to worry
steps.this_screen: A check-in ladder and a three-step escalation, with what the shore contact sees
steps.what_it_hands_on: Puts a second person into the safety system

steps.title: On-water glance display
steps.state_before: The screen must be readable with gloves in sunlight
steps.this_screen: Speed, depth, gate countdown and fuel on one glance, plus the return plan
steps.what_it_hands_on: The skipper does not touch the app again until the gate reopens

steps.title: Overdue: drift datum and search boxes
steps.state_before: No contact at 15:52; the shore contact has to act
steps.this_screen: Drift datum, three search boxes with probabilities and sweep times
steps.what_it_hands_on: The shore side of the same data the boat was using

steps.title: Fuel and range planner
steps.state_before: 36 L aboard, a long drift planned and wind forecast to build
steps.this_screen: Three fuel scenarios with the reserve shown as untouchable
steps.what_it_hands_on: Answers 'can I stay out for one more drift?' before it is asked at sea

steps.title: Harbour office e-ink noticeboard
steps.state_before: The harbour needs to know who is out and who is late
steps.this_screen: A public e-ink board with the fleet, the notices and the gate times
steps.what_it_hands_on: Makes the check-in data useful to people who are not on the boat

steps.title: Season debrief
steps.state_before: The season ends with three close calls and no pattern view
steps.this_screen: Monthly distance, forecast error trend and three rules adopted
steps.what_it_hands_on: Feeds the next season's planning, which is where case-01 begins again

shared_facts.bank_gate: crossable at 2.50 m or more: 02:15-08:10 and 14:55-20:20
shared_facts.plan: launch 06:25 · cross out 06:35 at 3.71 m · 17.6 nm and 326 min on the ground · cross back 14:58 at 2.55 m · alongside 15:08
shared_facts.fuel: 36 L in two tanks, plan 19.5 L, reserve 7.2 L, 12 kn headwind case 22.9 L
